description: Unofficial Minecraft 26.3 (Fabric) port of CircuitLord's Reactive Music

mods.name: Reactive Music Fork
mods.description: A fork of Reactive Music by CircuitLord, ported to 26.3 by Italo. Makes Minecraft's music dynamic and reactive, with songs from songpacks in the resourcepacks folder. The fork was made with AI: all of its changes to the code and the text. The icon is the original's. Full credits and more about the AI use in CREDITS_reactivemusic.txt inside the jar.

releases.notes:
Changes since 1.6.0:

- Says how AI was used in the fork, in the README, the Mod Menu description and the credits file inside the jar. The mod works the same.

mods.name: Reactive Music Fork
mods.description: A fork of Reactive Music by CircuitLord, ported to 26.3 by Italo. Makes Minecraft's music dynamic and reactive, with songs from songpacks in the resourcepacks folder.

releases.notes:
Changes since 1.5.0:

- Now called Reactive Music Fork in game, so it isn't taken for the original. The mod id (`reactivemusic`), config, `/reactivemusic` command and songpacks are the same, and it still can't be installed next to the original.
- New `firstSong` and `firstSongStart` for an entry: a song that plays the first time the entry plays after the mod is installed, from any point of it. It counts as played once it has been heard for 10 seconds.
- Songs from another pack are also found when Prism Launcher turned that pack off (`Some Pack.zip.disabled`). Before, such a song was found when the songpack loaded but couldn't be opened to play.
- A song that fails to open is no longer tried again on every tick.

mods.name: Reactive Music
mods.description: Refactors Minecraft's music to be dynamic and reactive, with songs from songpacks in the resourcepacks folder. Unofficial port to 26.3 by Italo.

releases.notes:
Changes since 1.4.0:

- Songs can be ogg files as well as mp3.
- A songpack can play Minecraft's own songs straight from the game files (`minecraft:music/game/sweden`), where no resource pack can swap them.
- A songpack can play songs from another zip in the `resourcepacks` folder (`Some Pack.zip/assets/.../song.ogg`), even when that pack isn't enabled. A missing pack gets one warning in the songpack list.
- New events: `CREATIVE`, and `BOSSBAR=` for one boss bar at a time, like `BOSSBAR=entity.minecraft.wither` or `BOSSBAR=event.minecraft.raid`.
- An entry whose songs are all missing is skipped instead of silencing the entries below it.
- A song that can't be read is skipped. Before, it stopped all music until the game restarted.

mods.name: Reactive Music
mods.description: Refactors Minecraft's music to be dynamic and reactive, with songs from songpacks in the resourcepacks folder. Unofficial port to 26.3 by Italo.

releases.notes:
Changes since 1.3.5:

- No songs come with the mod anymore, so the jar went from 281 MB to under 1 MB. Songs come from songpacks in the `resourcepacks` folder; the first one that loads plays until you pick another with `/reactivemusic`. With no songpack, Minecraft's own music plays.
- The songpack templates with songs are replaced by a template folder with only the config, in `docs/songpack-template`.

releases.notes:
Changes since the original 1.3.5:

- Runs on Minecraft 26.3, Fabric only. Needs Fabric API.
- Music other mods play through the game, like Naraka's boss fights and its dimension, plays again, and Reactive Music fades out under it the way it does for jukeboxes. Before, cancelling the game's music manager also stopped Naraka's boss music from fading and moving to the next phase.
- Discs from other mods fade the music out too.
- Riding a raft or a chest boat counts as BOAT again.
- Between songs the song player no longer keeps a whole processor core busy.
- No more "Unsupported control type: Master Gain" errors in the log.

The config is still `config/ReactiveMusic.json5`, and songpacks still go in `resourcepacks`.
